middle_investigation.root_cause_explanation: MIDDLE standardized distance spike is caused by near-zero training std dev on feature(s) [47, 56, 48]. For example, feature_47 (3D Joint-Angle Cosines [45..54]) has train std = 0.000718. When dividing unstandardized difference (1.5917) by near-zero std, the standardized term inflates to 2213.37. The unstandardized Euclidean train-to-test distance for MIDDLE is only 2.5386.

root_cause_summary.MIDDLE: Primary Cause: MIDDLE standardized distance spike is caused by near-zero training std dev on feature(s) [47, 56, 48]. For example, feature_47 (3D Joint-Angle Cosines [45..54]) has train std = 0.000718. When dividing unstandardized difference (1.5917) by near-zero std, the standardized term inflates to 2213.37. The unstandardized Euclidean train-to-test distance for MIDDLE is only 2.5386. Handedness: Train=RIGHT, Test=RIGHT.
root_cause_summary.TWO_FINGER: Primary Cause: Severe session shift in Finger Straightness and Joint-Angle Cosines (tr->te unstd dist: 2.5370). Confused with CLOSE and INDEX in test set. Handedness: Train=RIGHT, Test=LEFT.
root_cause_summary.THREE_FINGER: Primary Cause: High feature overlap with TWO_FINGER and MIDDLE. Test session shifted into TWO_FINGER feature space (sub-1NN acc with MIDDLE: 97.5%). Handedness: Train=LEFT, Test=RIGHT.
root_cause_summary.FOUR_FINGERS_vs_STOP: Primary Cause: Feature space overlap. 100% of test FOUR_FINGERS samples are closer to STOP train centroid than FOUR_FINGERS train centroid. Sub-problem 1-NN acc is only 38.0%. Top separating features are 2D Y-coordinates (features 14, 12, 10), reflecting height variation during static posture.
root_cause_summary.Handedness_Effects: Handedness flips between Train and Test exist for several classes (e.g. RIGHT in Train vs LEFT in Test), contributing to coordinate system asymmetries in 2D landmark features [0..39].
root_cause_summary.Final_Recommendation: B. Session/pose variation & C. Data collection consistency problem. The 68-D v2 feature extractor accurately reflects anatomical landmarks, but individual session recording styles and handedness shifts create held-out session variance. Next recommended action: Standardize gesture collection protocols or explore hyperparameter tuning/domain-invariant feature normalization.
